grounding.derivation: The public API promises to append an entry and await its decided log index. Wire identity associates the forwarded entry with the index actually assigned by the leader. Superseded documentation explicitly permits abandoning an uncertain operation after leadership change; it does not authorize successful completion for another entry. The obligation checks successful identity correspondence, not eventual commitment or mandatory supersession.
grounding.applicability: A public append_notify operation and its actual completion within the same configured log; assignment produced by captured code and no compaction.
alternatives: Success after leader change is permitted if the same proposed entry was adopted and decided.

claims.description: When Storage::write_atomically returns Err, the storage state exposed to its caller must equal the pre-call state, and a later independent successful transaction must not commit operations retained from the failed call.

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities

grounding.derivation: Storage::write_atomically explicitly requires all operations or rollback, with Err assumed rolled back to state before the call. PersistentStorage implements this trait and propagates entry serialization errors as Err without an advertised poisoning restriction. Public reads immediately after return test the state guarantee; a later unrelated transaction tests whether failed operations remain pending. The core relies on this backend during sync, but the obligation stays at the storage interface.
grounding.applicability: Direct public calls to the captured persistent backend using a trait-conforming entry with a controlled serializer error.
alternatives: Dropping and reopening may restore state, but that is not the stated return-time rollback guarantee.

formation.explanation: Proposals are buffered/forwarded or accepted by the leader. A new leader first gathers per-node Promises in its ballot, chooses highest accepted round and longest corresponding suffix, and synchronizes a prepare quorum history. In Accept, flushed local writes and qualified follower Accepted reports populate per-node prefix lengths. context.explanation: Caller-driven BLE ticks select ballots; explicit takeover also invokes handle_leader. A strictly newer ballot resets leader aggregation and stores a promise. A follower Prepare may acquire newer authority, or reacquire the same ballot only during recovery. Higher promised ballots reject old messages; accept sequence gaps request recovery and outdated sequences are ignored. Recovery reloads durable context and requests Prepare. Decided StopSign seals the current log and caller starts a new instance with transferred application history.

connection.explanation: Ballot election is not a decision quorum. Promises and persisted accepted history constrain new leader formation; batching is flushed before promises, old accepted indexes are reset at a new self ballot, and phase/ballot/sequence checks qualify later support. Buffered proposals are appended only after preparation and only without accepted reconfiguration; followers forward buffered proposals after sync when no StopSign exists. Same-ballot reconnect resynchronizes a peer using Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync rather than treating it as ready solely from connectivity.

items.rationale:
The accepted requirement is a successful append_notify result identifying its own proposed entry, not mandatory progress or mandatory Superseded. Public handle contract promises the entry's decided index; Superseded documentation permits uncertain failure but does not permit success for another value. I reviewed the fixed plan and harness under direct-checks/8c4dc87dc3104a0ab63e5a71d28e1a3a and the stdout/stderr and parsed monitor record for f6b6e1f52baa4f8991b6320420cee535. Compilation and the real test completed. Setup asserts three unique configured nodes, leader 1 in Accept, empty accepted/decided logs and drained link queues. This occurs before the selected request, so it does not remove the investigated overlap. Core instances are moved into real actors. The only executor adapter delegates to tokio spawn/sleep through the documented AsyncRuntime extension point. The application owns transport; one FIFO per directed link is used in both prefix and fault phase. After setup, node 1 outbound messages cannot be delivered until explicit release of 1->2; no fabricated Assignments or modified protocol messages occur. Node 2's actual tagged request reaches node 1 and produces an actual Assigned plus AcceptDecide containing 101. That old suffix cannot reach nodes 2 or 3 before their replacement decision, because every delivery uses the same link policy. The new leader is formed through public try_become_leader and real Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync interactions with nodes 2 and 3; large valid timeout configuration prevents irrelevant timer elections without replacing protocol logic. Events and outgoing channels are drained; setup asserts prerequisites rather than relying on process PASS.

The retained events correlate EntryId 43db97b7-53d4-47c6-a7b0-9cf04c2eb13a: admitted value 101; real assignment prefix length 1 in ballot number 1; old outbound delivered count 0 guaranteed by the single delivery policy; replacement Decided(202) at the origin in ballot number 2 while the target future is still pending; then the actual future returns Ok(1), and public read_decided_suffix(0) returns Decided(202). The fixed old_outbound_delivered field is a driver-policy invariant, not a separately sampled counter; inspection confirms all post-setup source-1 links are blocked until after replacement. The old acceptance diagnostic is derived from an emitted AcceptDecide inspected for value 101. The returned position is an accepted-prefix length, so k-1 is the corresponding zero-based index, matching append_tracked and core read classification. The measured value is read from the actual origin actor's core storage through a public API, not inferred from the assignment or the proposed replacement. Stable op_id correlates the single target future independently of value; exact wire EntryId additionally links admission/assignment prerequisites and is asserted in the harness. No ambiguity or parse errors appear in the retained monitor record.

The implication requires observed_value == admitted.proposed only when the independently observed future result is successful. It therefore detects 202 != 101 without treating an error, pending call, timeout or changed ballot alone as a defect. Whole-link release preserves FIFO and delivers any preceding traffic; core old-ballot rejection can protect log consistency while the runtime consumes a stale assignment. Source ordering explains the observation: record_assignment matches EntryId without current-ballot validation; until receipt the origin has no assigned ballot to supersede; afterward drain_notifiers chooses index<=decided before comparing ballots. This source-supported cause is consistent with the real-producer endpoint witness. The semantic review finds no correspondence issue in this scoped comparison; controller assessment, not this label or process PASS, owns confirmation.

Explained alternatives: EntryId correlation blocks unrelated calls but does not bind the accepted position to the value occupying it after a new ballot. The ballot-based Superseded branch works when assignment is already present and a tick observes changed promise before a replacement becomes decided; the captured repository test exercises that different schedule. New leaders may legitimately adopt the old entry, so ballot change is insufficient for violation; this check directly observes a different value instead.
items.report_title: 旧任期分配消息导致写入被错误确认
items.report_answer: 三节点同一配置中，101 的真实分配消息被延迟；新主节点随后在同一位置决定了 202。释放保持链路 FIFO 顺序的旧消息后，101 的 append_notify 返回 Ok(1)，但原节点读取到的是 Decided(202)。这验证的是客户端完成关联错误，不是两个节点决定了冲突日志。

items.rationale:
Reviewed the fixed plan and harness under direct-checks/66acce1428c3477f8a6c0f0d1ea19ee1, version-1 claim/binding records, execution eb1ca4d437f64ec8882a7005a78fb321 and its raw CA_EVENT lines and monitor correlations. The Storage trait explicitly requires every operation or rollback and states that Err has restored pre-call state. The captured PersistentStorage implementation has ordinary Serialize bounds, propagates serialization errors with ?, and documents no mandatory discard/poisoning rule for a returned Err. A deterministic serializer that returns a normal error for one selected entry is an applicable use of that interface; it does not patch the backend, inject a fabricated successful return, or invoke undefined behavior. Nonselected values serialize as u64 and deserialize through the newtype; successful readback of initial entry 7 establishes this path. The database is unique within the authorized clean workspace, opened through PersistentStorageConfig::with_path and closed before cleanup, with no concurrent access or OS fault.

The admitted transaction starts from actual observed length 1, promise ballot number 1 and entry 7. Its input operations are SetPromise(ballot number 2), AppendEntry(11), then AppendEntry(999). The error event records the actual returned Err and actual invocation of the selected failing serializer, with text selected entry cannot be serialized. Both formal comparisons share this operation identity and causally preceding error event. The first reads live get_log_len after return and observes 2 != 1. Its promise remains 1 and first entry 7; those contrary observations are retained and show that initial persisted metadata was not changed merely because the cached cursor changed. The later call contains only SetDecidedIndex(0), returns Ok, and is unwrapped before the later result event. That event observes database promise number 2 != pre-call 1 and entries [7,11]. The independent-completed diagnostic is not a global prerequisite because it follows the immediate result, but the fixed driver and retained success event establish its execution and completion before the second result. No result-selected inputs or adaptive policy are used. The chosen identity is the single failed transaction, not its changed length or ballot. Promise comparison projects only ballot number, sufficient to witness inequality here because the failed transaction changes that component while the independent call cannot write any promise.

The first discrepancy is live backend state: get_log_len uses next_log_key, not a count inferred by the test. The second is database state through get_promise, and the readback after closing and reopening additionally reports length 2, promise 2 and entries [7,11]. Reopen is diagnostic support for persisted leakage after the later successful transaction, not evidence that the first Err immediately persisted partial data. Source explains both outcomes: prior helpers queue batch operations and increment next_log_key; the later serializer error exits before mem::take, leaving both cursor and pending batch. The next write_atomically consumes that retained batch together with its own operation. This confirms the original local-state/retained-batch discriminator rather than a substituted database-atomicity hypothesis.

Existing protections do not contradict the scoped comparison: one RocksDB commit can be atomic while the wrong earlier operations are retained for that commit; dropping/reopening immediately after Err might discard volatile pending state but is not the promised return-time rollback; core protocol paths panic on storage Err, so the test deliberately does not infer continued live core execution or a cluster endpoint. The mock atomic-storage adapter fails before its entire memory batch, so it does not exercise this mid-preparation serializer path. Parsing has no errors, both result comparisons are complete, and no issue was found in correspondence within the accepted scope.
items.report_title: 持久存储返回错误后仍保留失败事务的状态
items.report_answer: 序列化返回 Err 后，公开读取的日志长度从 1 变成 2。随后仅设置 decided index 的独立事务，提交了失败事务中的 promise=2 和条目 11，重新打开数据库后仍可读到。该结果限定为 Storage 接口回滚违约，未证明集群级安全破坏。
